purpose: This links a parabola to its roots. You lift the curve with c and see the roots meet and then vanish from the real line. They are not gone: they reappear as a pair of complex numbers on the plane below.

stops.title: Two pictures
stops.text: Top: the parabola y = x^2 - 2x + c. The yellow dot is its lowest point (the vertex), and green dots mark where it crosses the x-axis. Bottom: the roots on a number line that grows into the complex plane. Drag the vertex up and down.
stops.try: After you answer the prediction in step 1, drag the yellow dot upward.

stops.title: Slide c
stops.text: c lifts or lowers the whole curve. The readout gives the vertex, the discriminant D and the roots. In steps 1, 3 and 4 the slider stays locked until you finish the question in the panel.
stops.try: Slide c from 0 up to 7 and watch the green dots come together.

stops.title: Sweep c
stops.text: Plays the whole slide for you, from c = -3 up to c = 9 over about seven seconds. Watch D go from positive to zero to negative, and the green dots go from two to one to none on the top graph.
stops.try: Press it and watch the bottom picture while the top dots disappear.

stops.title: What Next does
stops.text: Step 1 asks you to predict, then unlocks c. Step 2 explains the discriminant. Step 3 solves x^2 - 2x + 5 = 0 piece by piece. Step 4 asks you to place the second root on the plane, then slide c again.

stops.title: Solve it piece by piece
stops.text: In step 3 you answer each part of the quadratic formula, then check the root and complete the square. When you find the root, the bottom number line turns into the complex plane with real part across and imaginary up.
stops.try: Answer the first piece, then press Next piece.

stops.title: Try practice problems
stops.text: Eight short problems. Each shows a quadratic, asks about its roots, and reveals the graph after you answer. Nothing is saved. Press Back to the lesson to return.
stops.try: Start practice and see the graph appear after your first answer.

stops.title: Quick check
stops.text: A few questions at the end. A wrong answer explains itself.

teacher: Project step 4 and ask: where do the roots go when the curve lifts off the axis? Students often say they disappear. Slide c up and show the pair at x = 1 moving up and down in mirror image. Ask why the real part stays 1.
